sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Orlando?
sections.html:
Orange County bills it. Orlando levies its own city millage, but the Property Appraiser sets values and the Orange County Tax Collector mails one combined bill and collects the money.

The City of Orlando says it receives about 35 cents of each property tax dollar. The rest goes to Orange County, Orange County Public Schools, the St. Johns water management district and the library system. A seller therefore deals with county offices for everything that touches the bill, and with the city for services, permits and its budget.

  • Orange County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, mailing address
  • Orange County Tax Collector: bills, payments, delinquent taxes, certificates
  • City of Orlando: sets its own millage rate and budget

sections.h2: What is the City of Orlando millage rate?
sections.html:
The city's tax page prints its rate as 0.00665 in its worked table, which is 6.65 mills, and it states the rate has stayed unchanged for more than a decade. The Property Appraiser publishes the final millage for each taxing body by year, so check that site for the current combined rate on a specific address.

Millage is a rate per $1,000 of taxable value, and the city's rate is only one line on the bill. County, school and district levies add to it, and special assessments sit on top. Ask the Tax Collector for the bill of the property you plan to sell, since the lines vary by neighborhood and by special taxing district.

sections.h2: What else does the city say about itself?
sections.html:
The city's tax page describes more than 340,000 residents and says nearly 50,000 people arrived in the last five years. It reports a AAA credit rating from Fitch Ratings and strong reserves, and it reads that the existing 3 percent cap has limited the effect of rising values on long-time homeowners.

For a seller, the figures that matter are practical ones. Roughly six in ten Orlando residents rent, so many buyers of a house here are investors, and the home's tax history is a talking point in any offer. Share the Tax Collector's account page with a buyer, show the exemption status, and mention any special district lines that appear on the bill.

sections.h2: How big is Orlando and who owns homes here?
sections.html:
QuickFacts has Orlando at 333,888 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 8.4 percent since the 2020 base. The land area is 110.62 square miles, and fewer than four in ten homes are lived in by their owners.

sections.h2: When are Orlando property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed by November 1, the full amount is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1. Early payment earns 4 percent off in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.

The Tax Collector counts the date it receives payment, so a March 31 postmark on April 3 delivery is late. Delinquent bills carry a 3 percent minimum charge plus advertising cost. A certificate sale follows on or before June 1, with interest bids starting at 18 percent. Escrow customers should note that the lender may hold the bill and the owner may receive only a copy.

sections.h2: How do Save Our Homes and the homestead exemption affect an Orlando seller?
sections.html:
Homestead cuts taxable value by up to $50,000, and Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in a homestead's assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or inflation. The Department of Revenue's chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024.

The city's page shows the effect with its sample of a median home bought a decade ago, which stays far below the assessed value of a similar home bought today. A sale ends that protection: change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1. A seller who moves within Florida may be able to carry part of the benefit to a new homestead by filing the portability form with the exemption application by March 1, within three years of abandoning the old homestead.

sections.h2: What does the City of Orlando spend its share on?
sections.html:
The city lists police with more than 900 first responders, fire and rescue with more than 600, 123 parks, 19 neighborhood centers, 900 miles of streets and 1,200 miles of sidewalks. It also reports more than 500 traffic signals.

Those services shape what a buyer sees when touring a home, from park access to street maintenance. The page states that a share of the budget pays for free pools and neighborhood center programs. It also warns that changes to state homestead taxation could reduce city revenue in fiscal years 2028 and 2029. Because the page discusses a statewide property tax amendment on the November 2026 ballot, ask the Property Appraiser or Tax Collector how any approved change applies to your bill before relying on older figures.

sections.h2: What should I do about unpaid taxes before selling in Orlando?
sections.html:
Ask the Orange County Tax Collector for a payoff, and clear any delinquent amount at or before closing. If you ever used the homestead tax deferral, ask the Tax Collector how a deferred balance is repaid at sale.

  • Check whether a tax certificate was sold on the parcel
  • After April 1, pay with certified or cashier's funds, money order or cash in person
  • If two years have passed on an unredeemed certificate, act at once, since a tax deed application can follow
  • Make sure any lender escrow account has paid the current year

Cash buyers can often close fast on a property with a tax lien, and the lien is paid from the proceeds. Compare that with the cost of a listing and repairs.

faqs.q: Does Orlando collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Orange County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city's levy. Orlando sets its own millage rate, and the city says it keeps about 35 cents of each dollar paid.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate in Orlando?
faqs.a: The city's tax page shows 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and says the rate has been unchanged for more than a decade. Your bill also carries county, school and district levies.

faqs.q: When do Orlando property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The full amount is due by March 31, and a payment must reach the Tax Collector by then. A 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost follow.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap carry over when I sell in Orlando?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, filed by March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I check my tax bill before listing a house in Orlando?
faqs.a: Search the Orange County Tax Collector's records by owner name, parcel ID or address, and use the Property Appraiser's parcel record for value and exemptions.
